    Construction

    Rim cut whole from one standard 1-3/4 in Honduran mahogany body blank, all from the top face in one setup, for a 2.0 in body at the edge (the same as the C-75): 8 mm walls that the top glues to directly, a 12 × 8 mm glue ledge for the back routed in place of kerfed linings, solid neck and tail blocks, open-top mortise for the set neck's tenon. The neck continues as a tongue under the fingerboard extension over the neck block, and its tenon drops through a notch in the top, so the neck goes on last. Every part is cut on a 3-axis router in one or two setups. Spruce top carved as flat planes, graduated light (about 150 g): falls 2.8 mm at the plateau rising to 3.2 mm at the skirt, a 3.5 mm hexagonal bridge plateau, 141 mm wide so the 135 mm Gretsch base sits flat on it, inside an arch zone that runs on into both upper bouts (symmetric below the waist, following the outline and the cutaway above it), 17 facets in all, with the two soundholes in the side facets beside the bridge (each with a 12 mm lip underneath to keep the air resonance about 127 Hz in the shallower box) and a flat skirt outside it that lands on the rim. A 5 × 6 mm ring beam under the base's feet and two 6 × 5 mm parallel tone bars with scalloped ends run under the plateau's long sides, and a 6 × 5 mm cross bar braces the flat upper bout from the neck block. Top is quartersawn Sitka spruce, dyed black under the shellac, with a quarter-inch undyed band left around the edge as a faux binding. Back is quartersawn bigleaf maple, arched 22 mm over the same footprint as the top (deep enough to win back most of the air the thinner rim gives up): 13 flat facets rising to a centre ridge, with a flat border, glued on and stiff enough to reflect energy back into the top without braces.

    No pickguard. An EMG 91 active floating humbucker hangs from a bracket under the fingerboard extension, and its lead drops into the body through a 6 mm hole hidden under the board. A stacked volume/tone pot with a concentric knob, a stereo output jack and a battery door share a 2 mm access plate on the flat treble lower-bout face of the rim. The 9 V slides end-first into a sleeve behind the door, so a battery change is a quarter-turn and no screws; the plate itself comes off only for wiring work, through the 84 × 30 mm window behind it. Being active, the EMG needs no string or tailpiece ground.
